info.title: Nodal Agent Bridge API
info.description:
Local HTTP API of the Nodal agent bridge (`nodal-agent.mjs`). It lets AI agents, scripts and other programs drive a running Nodal window (web or desktop): place and wire parts, draw, manage pages and symbols, run the electrical rules check, read nets, export and take screenshots. Each change shows up live on the canvas with the agent's own cursor and stays off the user's undo history.

The bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Start it with `node nodal-agent.mjs` (download: https://jpmarcelino.github.io/nodal/nodal-agent.mjs), then open Nodal and choose File -> AI agent link. All circuit operations are JSON-RPC style calls to `POST /rpc` with `{method, params}`; pick a method from the examples list. The same methods are available as MCP tools (`claude mcp add nodal -- node nodal-agent.mjs mcp`).

Nodal agent API. You drive a live Nodal window: every edit appears on the user's canvas as you make it, with your own cursor and an activity log. Your work is independent of the user's selection, tool, page and viewport: always pass explicit ids, coordinates and (optionally) a page; nothing here reads what the user clicked. Edits you make are not on the user's undo stack (use history.undo for yours).

Workflow: session.start {name, goal} first, then build, then session.done {summary}. While you are working the user may be prevented from editing what you made (the guard; the user decides). Use session.say to narrate, doc.screenshot to look at the result, check.run to verify wiring.

Coordinates: world pixels, x right, y DOWN. The grid is doc.settings.grid (default 10); keep parts and wire points on it. A typical 2-pin part (resistor) is 60–80 px long. Rotation is 0/90/180/270 clockwise.

Items (doc.items, keyed by id): component (a placed symbol: symbol, x, y = its centre, rot, flipX, ref like R1, value like 10k, props), wire (a, b endpoints + pts bends), junction (solder dot x, y), shape (kind rect|zone|ellipse|polygon|line|arrow|text|image|ink|callout|frame, box x y w h, styling). Wire endpoints: {kind:'port', comp, port} | {kind:'junction', id} | {kind:'free', x, y}.

Wiring: prefer wires.connect with port targets ({ref:'R1', port:'2'} or {comp:id, port:'name or id'}); it routes orthogonally around parts and makes junctions where you land on a wire. components.ports tells you each pin's id, name and absolute position. Nets also join by name: place 'net-label' / 'gnd' / 'vcc' symbols with the same value on several pins.

Pages: a document has one or more pages; methods taking 'page' default to your working page (session.setPage), never the user's page.

Symbols: symbols.list / symbols.get give the library (ids like 'resistor', 'capacitor', 'dc-source', 'gnd', 'vcc', 'net-label', 'opamp'). symbols.create adds a custom symbol drawn in the symbol DSL: one command per line — W w (stroke width), SC colour, FC colour, DA 1|0 (dashed), L x1 y1 x2 y2 … (polyline), G … (closed polygon, GF filled, GB background-filled), R x y w h [rx] (RF, RB), C cx cy r (CF, CB), E cx cy rx ry, A cx cy r a1 a2 (arc, degrees clockwise from +x), P <svg path> (PF, PB), T x y size s|m|e text. Ports: 'name:x,y name2:x,y' in symbol-local px (origin top-left).

Batching: batch {calls:[{method, params}]} runs many edits as ONE step (one undo, one repaint); later calls can use ids from earlier ones via "$0.id" / "$2.ids.0" strings (result of call #n, dotted path).

Errors come back as {error:{code, message}}. Read-only methods never change anything.

get.summary: Bridge status and whether a Nodal window is linked
The method catalog (guide and every method with its parameters)

post.summary: Call a method on the linked Nodal window
post.description: Runs one of the 107 methods. Calls run one at a time, in order. Use `batch` to apply several calls in one go (later calls can refer to earlier results as `$0.id`). Waits up to NODAL_AGENT_WAIT_MS (15 s) for a Nodal window to link.

Call_wires_path.description: Draws a wire exactly through given points (no routing); ends snap to pins, junctions or wires lying on them. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_wires_reroute.title: wires.reroute
Call_wires_reroute.description: Re-routes wires around parts (all wires on the page when no ids). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_wires_junction.title: wires.junction
Call_wires_junction.description: Joins wires that cross or meet at a point with a solder dot (or adds a free junction). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_wires_unsolder.title: wires.unsolder
Call_wires_unsolder.description: Removes a junction (the wires through it stay joined as one) or disconnects a pin. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_wires_label.title: wires.label
Call_wires_label.description: Names a wire (its net) and places the label. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_wires_deletePart.title: wires.deletePart
Call_wires_deletePart.description: Deletes one bend (node) or one segment of a wire: an end segment shortens it, a middle one splits it in two. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

index.description: node index (0 = end a) or segment index

Call_shapes_add.title: shapes.add
Call_shapes_add.description: Adds a shape. Boxes use x, y, w, h; line / arrow use from / to (points or {id} to glue to an item) and optional bends; polygon / path use points; text uses text and fontSize; callout uses text and anchor {x,y} or {id}; image uses src (data URL); ink uses points with optional pressure p. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

props.description: any ShapeItem fields (stroke, fill, fillOpacity, strokeWidth, dash, radius, fontSize, textColor, bold, route, headEnd…)

Call_shapes_presets.title: shapes.presets
Call_shapes_presets.description: Lists the shape presets (flowchart, arrows, basic).

Call_shapes_addPreset.title: shapes.addPreset
Call_shapes_addPreset.description: Adds a preset shape (e.g. a flowchart decision). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_shapes_connect.title: shapes.connect
Call_shapes_connect.description: Draws a connector (arrow or line) glued between two items, so it follows them. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_shapes_note.title: shapes.note
Call_shapes_note.description: Adds a callout pointing at items (or a point) with text — handy to explain your work. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_shapes_toPath.title: shapes.toPath
Call_shapes_toPath.description: Turns rectangles, ellipses and unattached lines into editable paths (polygons with curves). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_symbols_list.title: symbols.list
Call_symbols_list.description: Library symbols (built-in, the user's and the document's), filtered.

query.description: words in name, id, category or keywords

Call_symbols_get.title: symbols.get
Call_symbols_get.description: A symbol's full definition: size, pins (id, name, local x, y, side), fields, prefix, types, and its DSL source.

Call_symbols_create.title: symbols.create
Call_symbols_create.description: Creates (or replaces) a custom symbol from DSL source; it is stored in the document and, optionally, in the user's library. Returns its id. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_symbols_fromSvg.title: symbols.fromSvg
Call_symbols_fromSvg.description: Creates a custom symbol from SVG markup (its drawing), with pins you name. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_symbols_fromItems.title: symbols.fromItems
Call_symbols_fromItems.description: Turns items into a new symbol; with replace, they are swapped for one instance of it. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_symbols_delete.title: symbols.delete
Call_symbols_delete.description: Removes a custom symbol from the user's library (parts using it keep their copy).

Call_symbols_importLibrary.title: symbols.importLibrary
Call_symbols_importLibrary.description: Adds the symbols of a Nodal library file (format 'nodal-library') to the user's library.

library.description: any — library object or its JSON text

overwrite.description: replace symbols with the same id

Call_symbols_exportLibrary.title: symbols.exportLibrary
Call_symbols_exportLibrary.description: The user's library as a Nodal library file (to save or share).

Call_nets_list.title: nets.list
Call_nets_list.description: Electrical nets: name, label names, wires and pins (ref.port).

Call_nets_of.title: nets.of
Call_nets_of.description: The net of a pin or wire.

Call_check_run.title: check.run
Call_check_run.description: Runs the electrical rules check: unconnected pins, duplicate refs, shorts, loose ends… (issues the user chose to ignore are listed apart).

Call_check_ignore.title: check.ignore
Call_check_ignore.description: Marks rule-check issues as ignored (or not). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_history_undo.title: history.undo
Call_history_undo.description: Undoes your last step (only yours; refused if the user has changed the same items since). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_history_redo.title: history.redo
Call_history_redo.description: Redoes your last undone step. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_history_steps.title: history.steps
Call_history_steps.description: Your steps so far (labels, item counts), newest last.

Call_versions_save.title: versions.save
Call_versions_save.description: Saves a named version of the circuit in its version history.

Call_versions_list.title: versions.list
Call_versions_list.description: Saved versions of the open circuit.

Call_versions_restore.title: versions.restore
Call_versions_restore.description: Opens a saved version in place of the circuit (the current state is saved as a version first). (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)

Call_symbolEditor_open.title: symbolEditor.open
Call_symbolEditor_open.description: Opens the user's symbol editor page on a symbol (or a new one). UI action.

Call_symbolEditor_close.title: symbolEditor.close
Call_symbolEditor_close.description: Closes the symbol editor page without saving.

Call_batch.title: batch
Call_batch.description: Runs several calls as ONE step (one undo step, one repaint). Strings like "$0.id" refer to earlier results (call index, dotted path). Stops at the first error and undoes the whole batch. (Changes the circuit; undoable with history.undo.)
